answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments bind each agent to a unique Merkle-rooted identity while a VRF sortition emits a non-interactive signal. A zero-knowledge verifiable delay function forces any cloning attempt to expend sequential time proportional to the staked collateral and the protocol slashes the stake for missed proofs. Game-theoretic analysis yields negative expected attack utility when the slashing penalty exceeds stake multiplied by the raven-adjusted zephyr latency, establishing a robust Nash equilibrium.
